answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independently checked outputs show fraud or collusion. A sybil attacker must therefore acquire and lock real capital for every fake identity, rather than minting names for free; scaling the attack raises the cost and risks forfeiture. In a dune of cheap identities, onyx-backed stakes make abuse costly, though they cannot prevent a wealthy attacker from trying; the nadir is reached when honest checks are too weak to catch misconduct.
